Description:
A coil spring resting on a coaxial core, in two versions that differ by a tenth of a millimetre - which
is the point of the case.

The wire is a circle of radius 2 whose centre runs on a helix of radius 10 with pitch 8, three turns
(1080 degrees), so it fills the radial band 8..12 and reaches from z = -2 to z = 26.

  core       a cylinder of radius 8, z from 0 to 24. Its lateral face is EXACTLY tangent to the inner
             envelope of the wire, 10 - 2 = 8, so the two bodies touch along a helix and share no
             volume at all.
  thickCore  the same cylinder at radius 8.1. Now the two really overlap, in a thin sliver of the wire
             that is nowhere thicker than 0.1 radially.

The pair is the interesting part: the same union, once exactly at the tangency and once a hair past it.
The first must NOT merge the bodies, the second must.
Expected:
THE OPERANDS, in closed form. A screw motion has the same Jacobian r as plain cylindrical coordinates -
the lift is a shear and does not change it - so sweeping a profile through an angle Theta gives
V = Theta * A * rbar exactly:
  volume(coil)      = 6*pi * 4*pi * 10 = 240*pi^2 = 2368.7050563
  volume(core)      = pi*8^2*24        = 1536*pi  = 4825.4863159
  volume(thickCore) = pi*8.1^2*24  = 1574.64*pi   = 4946.8774560

AT THE TANGENCY, coilOnCore. The bodies touch along a helix and share no volume, so the union is TWO
separate solids - bodies that merely touch are not merged, which is this project's convention (decided
2026-08-10). Their volumes are those of the operands, unchanged, and together
  240*pi^2 + 1536*pi = 7194.1913722
An intersection here would have to be empty.

A TENTH PAST IT, coilOnThickCore. Raising the radius to 8.1 cuts a sliver off the inside of the wire, so
the union is now ONE solid. The overlap is the part of the wire with r <= 8.1, clipped to z in [0,24]:
  the unclipped part is 6*pi times the integral of r over the circular segment of the wire profile,
  and the two ends that stick out past z = 0 and z = 24 are taken off with the same argument as in
  HelicalCoilInsideCylinder - the integral over theta turns into the first moment of the segment:
    overlap = 6*pi*M - (pi/2)*N = 12.5903904, of which only 0.1245969 is the end correction
    with M = integral of r, and N = integral of r*|z|, over the segment {(r,z) in wire : r <= 8.1}
  volume(coilOnThickCore) = 240*pi^2 + 1574.64*pi - 12.5903904 = 7302.9921219

The sliver is thin - at r = 8.1 the segment is 1.2489996 tall and 0.1 wide - so the two unions differ by
about 1.5 percent in volume while differing completely in topology. That is what makes the pair a test:
a merge that fails to happen and a merge that must.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-26.

The case was recorded while the union threw an exception; it was fixed on 2026-08-10 and has returned
two solids ever since, which is correct - the bodies touch along a helix and share no volume. Its own
Status used to say "intersect STILL WRONG", but there has been no intersect call in the file for some
time, so that sentence pinned nothing. It is gone.

What the case now tests is the PAIR: at radius 8 the union must not merge, at radius 8.1 it must. Both
are checked against closed forms, see Expected.
Actual: solid.boolean intersect returns 2368.6613 - the complete coil, i.e. operand a - although the bodies only touch along a line and the intersection must be empty. See HelicalCoilDisjointCylinder.json for the canonical case.
Actual (before the fix): solid.boolean union failed with 'Error in the application.'.
